bias: Conditions are stable-to-improving versus Friday: yields eased back 4-5bp across the curve, oil extended its pullback (-5.5% since Friday), and equity vol (VIX) calmed to 15.6. The one clear deterioration is bond-market vol — MOVE broke above the 80 stress threshold for the first time in this series, even as everything else looks calm. Korea/memory (KOSPI, SK Hynix, Samsung) gave back roughly a third to a half of Friday's historic AI-capex rally, which reads as digestion of an extreme one-day move rather than a new negative catalyst.

counterargs.read: Today looks like consolidation rather than reversal: broad macro conditions (yields, oil, credit, equity vol) improved modestly versus Friday, and the sharp pullback in Korea/memory names reads as digestion of Friday's record +17.9% KOSPI melt-up rather than a fresh shock. The one genuine new development is MOVE crossing above 80 for the first time in this series — a bond-vol divergence from the calm equity tape that's worth monitoring even though it hasn't yet shown up anywhere else (credit spreads tightened, VIX fell). Net: the Friday AI-capex thesis isn't broken, but the one-day give-back plus the MOVE breach argue for smaller size and confirmation before adding, not for chasing the follow-through.
